Card Hand Toolkit — FAQ

#

New to the toolkit? Start with the Quick Start. For every class and interface, see the API Reference.

Getting started

#

Q: Which sections should I read first? A: After the Quick Start, read the Concepts in the API Reference, then the module guide for what you're building: Zones & Play for where cards go, Card Data & Decks for drawing and dealing, Card Visuals for how cards look, Interaction for hover, drag and tap, and Hands & Layout for the hands themselves.

Q: What’s safe to modify? A: Anything tagged [C] in the API Reference is intended for configuration. Types tagged [E] are designed for extension via interfaces/policies. Types tagged [L] are primarily informational.

Don't edit files inside Assets/CardHandToolkit/ (other than Config/, which the Setup Wizard creates for you). A toolkit update can replace them. Instead:

  • Change a prefab in your scene, such as the Player Hand or a zone, by editing the instance in the scene. Those changes are saved in your scene, not in the toolkit's prefab.
  • Use your own settings asset, such as a Fan Layout Profile, by creating one from Create ▸ Card Toolkit and assigning it in place of the shipped CHT_ one.
  • Change the prefab itself by making a Prefab Variant (right-click the prefab ▸ Create ▸ Prefab Variant) and using that instead.

Q: Do I have to use LineBoardZone and SingleSlotZone? A: No. They're examples of play zones. Use them as they are, or write your own by implementing ICardZone and IPlayResolver. The hands, deck and discard visuals are meant to be used as they are.

Interaction and decks

#

Q: How do I change what a card allows: hover, drag, select or target? A: Supply an IInteractionPolicy globally through Override Policy Asset on CardToolkitRuntime, or per zone through IInteractionPolicyProvider. Add CardInteractionOverride for individual cards. After changing game state that your policy reads, call InteractionController.RefreshAll() (or Refresh() for one card). See Permissions and policies.

Q: Can I block dragging on one specific card? A: Add Card Interaction Override to that card and tick Drag in Deny. Deny wins over Allow. If you change the masks at runtime, call Refresh() on that card's InteractionController. See IInteractionOverride / CardInteractionOverride.

Q: What happens when the deck is empty? A: Draw() asks the deck's IEmptyDeckPolicy to refill it. The default ReshuffleOnEmpty shuffles the discard pile back in; NoReshufflePolicy leaves it empty. If the policy can't refill it, EmptyEvent fires and Draw() returns only the cards it could draw, possibly none. See Decks.

Q: Can players reorder cards in their hand by dragging? A: Yes. Release inside the Player Hand's reorder band to move a card to that position. For a custom hand, implement IReorderBandZone; DragCard uses it to compute the insert index. See The Player Hand.

Q: How does hover differ between mouse and touch? A: In a focused hand, mouse-over or holding a finger on a card lifts it. Out of the hand, the mouse opens a preview after a short delay; touch opens it after a long press, and tapping the backdrop closes it. Tune timings and placement on the Hover Profile, assigned on CardToolkitRuntime. See Hover.

Troubleshooting

#

Q: Why does mouse hover flicker near the bottom of the screen? A: Check the Player Hand's Hover Anchor: its cyan gizmo line should be at or below the bottom edge of the screen, so a lifted card doesn't expose the next card under the pointer. Check its Reference Card if you've changed the card prefab's collider or scale. See HoverAnchor.

Q: I pressed Play and got "No CardToolkitRuntime found in scene". A: The scene you pressed Play from has no CHT_CardToolkitLoader. The Setup Wizard puts one in your Game scene. For any other scene with cards, copy the loader from your Game scene into it.

Q: The Console says "CardToolkitRuntime missing CardDatabase reference" (or CardFrameLibrary, HoverProfile, ICardVisualFactory). A: A field on the CHT_CardToolkitLoader in your scene is empty. Select the loader and assign the missing asset on its CardToolkitRuntime component, or run the Setup Wizard again on that scene with Use Existing. If the error is about HoverPolicyRuntime instead, that component is missing from the loader. Replace the loader with a fresh CHT_CardToolkitLoader prefab and run the Wizard on the scene.

Q: My cards' frame or back is plain white. A: Cards take their frame and back from the CardFrameLibrary at runtime, not from the card materials. Set its Default Frame and Default Card Back. The textures on CardFrontMat_User and CardBackMat_User only show in the editor.

Q: A card shows the wrong frame. A: Check the card's Frame Key. An empty key, or a key that doesn't match any entry in the CardFrameLibrary's Frames list, uses the Default Frame.

Q: My custom field never shows. A: Check that the same key is used in three places: the FieldToggle's Custom Key, the Card Skin's Enabled Custom Fields, and the key your ViewModel passes to SetCapability. Keys aren't case-sensitive. A key that's missing from the Card Skin logs a one-time warning in the Console.
